ga-house-1-2026-r-1.bio: In 2020 Mike was elected as State Representative for Georgia House District 1, which includes parts of Walker and all of Dade Counties. In 2022 and 2024, Mike was reelected as your State Representative.
ga-house-1-2026-r-1.name: Mike Cameron

ga-house-113-2026-d-2.bio: As your State Representative, I will be a progressive voice in the Georgia State House and a present, accountable partner here at home. I will work to lower the cost of living, expand access to quality and affordable healthcare, strengthen our public schools, and hold powerful corporations accountable when they put profits over people. You will see me at the grocery store, the park, church, neighborhood meetings, and local cookouts; listening, learning, and serving. Representation does not stop in Atlanta; it begins and ends in the community. In the spirit of my father's legacy, and guided by the values he passed down to me, I am proud to announce my candidacy for the Georgia House of Representatives in District 113.

ga-house-113-2026-d-1.bio: I have served as a local elected official where I have written resolutions and championed community priorities. As a lobbyist for the State of Georgia, I have written bills and testified on various issues affecting our communities. My work with Newton County Commission demonstrated my commitment to delivering results and understanding how to navigate the legislative process effectively. I believe in concrete action and will consistently report on the progress and outcomes of my efforts, ensuring transparency and trust.

ga-house-114-2026-d-1.bio: I am Michael Caw, a retired research and development technician, community volunteer, and proud resident of Newborn, Georgia. I am running for the Georgia House of Representatives to bring thoughtful, data-driven leadership and a neighbor's common sense to the State Capitol.

ga-house-114-2026-r-1.bio: Georgia might be ranked the number one state to do business, and that's great if you're a large corporation, but I'm focused on making Georgia the best place in the country to own and grow a small business. That means cutting red tape, making essential agencies more efficient, and pushing bold initiatives like eliminating the state income tax. Now is not the time for conservatives to be timid. We need leaders in Atlanta with real world experience who will fight for working families and main street—not just the big guys.
ga-house-114-2026-r-1.name: Brett Mauldin

ga-house-115-2026-r-1.bio: I'm running to ensure that responsible growth in our communities benefits residents, not just developers; that homeowners aren't priced out of their own neighborhoods; that our infrastructure, schools, and public safety measures keep pace with the growth; and that the needs of seniors and working families are respected and not overlooked. I believe that government should be accountable, practical, and deeply rooted in the real lives of the people it represents. My goal is straightforward: to be a voice you recognize, a leader you can reach, and a representative who shows up and gets the important work done.

ga-house-115-2026-d-1.bio: Elected to the Georgia General Assembly in 2020, Lewis-Ward partnered with the Gordon State College Foundation to establish an empowerment scholarship for women interested in American politics, aiming to address the under-representation of African American women in public office. In 2025, she established a second scholarship at Clayton State University to inspire future leaders in public service. She also secured a grant through a program administered by the GA Forestry Commission to increase urban tree canopy, directing resources to disadvantaged communities across her legislative district. Lewis-Ward helped secure almost $400,000 in the FY 2022 state budget for students in her district to participate in the American Association of Adapted Sports Program, and $39,000 for the startup of a Court Appointed Special Advocate (CASA) program in Henry County, GA. She also co-sponsored bipartisan legislation, 2021 HB 676, now signed into law, that provides legislative advisory oversight of state farmers' markets. In 2023, the House of Representatives passed HB 144, the George Burgess Act, introduced by Representative Lewis-Ward to strengthen the rights of adult wards under guardianship.

ga-senate-42-2026-r-1.bio: Grounded in faith, guided by the Constitution, and driven by a commitment to serve others, Bret is ready to lead with bold conservative leadership. He will bring the same discipline, grit, and determination he learned in the Marine Corps to the fight for faith, family, and freedom. Our families do not need more politics as usual, we need a conservative fighter. Bret Dunn is ready to bring bold, principled and unapologetic conservative leadership to the Senate. He will stand tall to fight for our values and deliver real conservative results.
ga-senate-42-2026-r-1.name: Bret A. Dunn

ga-senate-43-2026-d-2.bio: Formerly House Representative from District 113, she was suspended from her seat by Gov. Kemp due to her ongoing criminal case.

ga-senate-43-2026-d-3.bio: Senator Tonya P. Anderson, a Democrat, has served in the Georgia State Senate since 2016. She represents Senate District 43, which includes Rockdale County and portions of Dekalb, Gwinnett and Newton counties. Prior to serving as State Senator, she served as the 1st State Representative for House District 92. Prior to serving as a State Representative, she served as City Councilwoman and Mayor for the City of Lithonia.
ga-senate-43-2026-d-3.name: Tonya P Anderson

ga-house-118-2026-d-1.bio: I'm a Newton County homeowner, a mother, and a small business owner since 2012. I built my career by solving real problems for real people—helping organizations grow, leading strategy, and delivering outcomes. Now, I'm bringing that same results-driven approach to the State House—focused on what families in District 118 are living every day: cost of living pressures, school and youth outcomes, public safety, and healthcare.

ga-house-118-2026-d-2.bio: I'm stepping forward not just as a candidate—but as someone who believes in the power of change. For too long, many in our communities have felt unheard and unseen. I'm stepping forward because I believe our district deserves leadership that uplifts families, strengthens, protects our rights and stands firmly for justice for all. This moment is about rising together. It's about turning our challenges into purpose and our hopes into real progress for the people who call District 118 home. When we stand together, we can build a future where every voice matters and every family has the opportunity to thrive. I'm honored to take this step with you.
ga-house-118-2026-d-2.name: Sharonda Bell

ga-house-118-2026-r-1.bio: State Representative Clint Crowe represents the citizens of House District 118, which includes Butts County, as well as portions of Monroe and Newton counties. He was elected to the Georgia House of Representatives in 2020. Rep. Crowe is a second-generation realtor, and he has worked in the real estate industry for more than 20 years. Prior to running a real estate business, Rep. Crowe had a decade long career in law enforcement as a patrolman/field training officer and detective with a metro Atlanta police department.

ga-senate-11-2026-r-1.bio: In the State Senate, Sam will continue to modernize tax policies, improve incentives and remove outdated codes that create financial roadblocks for our local economies. He will continue to educate our legislators on the workforce challenges that rural Georgia faces and the regulations that are stifling our ability to thrive - from EPA to labor and water.
ga-senate-11-2026-r-1.name: Sam Watson

ga-senate-10-2026-d-2.bio: Katherine “Kate” Denny is a candidate for Georgia’s Senate District 10 in the 2026 General Election. With a platform focused on healthcare, education/childcare, wages, and housing, Kate brings nearly two decades of medical experience, having been a trauma nurse for nearly 20 years, and a lived understanding of the challenges facing working families across Georgia.

ga-senate-10-2026-d-4.name: Sylvester Smith III
ga-senate-10-2026-d-4.bio: Sylvester Smith is a father, community leader, data specialist, and lifelong advocate for District 10. He has lived, raised a family, and served across the district for decades. He has led civic organizations, strengthened youth programs, and represented District 10’s values at the local, county, and state levels. District 10 deserves safe communities, strong schools, revitalized corridors, and opportunities for every family. I’m running for State Senate to bring disciplined leadership, strategic thinking, and community-focused solutions to the Capitol.

ga-senate-10-2026-d-3.bio: Because of his background and efforts in the field of public health, The Honorable Larry Johnson was appointed in 2005 to chair the Health Disparities Subcommittee of the Health Steering Committee for NACo, the National Association of Counties. In 2008, he was appointed as Vice Chair of the NACo Health Steering Committee. The Health Steering Committee has jurisdiction, on a national policy level, over all matters pertaining to health care delivery and financing including: indigent care health, care for the uninsured, Medicaid, Medicare, long-term care, local public health programs, mental health, substance abuse and development disabilities.

ga-senate-10-2026-d-1.bio: A tireless champion for underserved communities, Gabrielle has directed over $3 million in resources and led initiatives that have impacted more than 60,000 lives. Her leadership has earned recognition from the Atlanta Business Chronicle’s 40 Under Forty, DeKalb County School District’s Difference Maker Award, Zeta Phi Beta’s Community Pillar Award, and the Georgia Federation of Business and Professional Women’s Young Professional of the Year.|

ga-senate-10-2026-r-1.bio: Running for GA Senate District 10 as a Republican.
ga-senate-10-2026-r-1.name: Furquan Stafford

ga-house-7-2026-r-1.name: Johnny Chastain
ga-house-7-2026-r-1.bio: I am tired of politicians that, while running, take positions on issues, make promises and statements [that they end up later breaking] and run a slash and burn campaign attacking their opponents. That's not me.  I won't do it.  I will, however, tell you where my core values come from, and how I will make decisions. Conservative Christian values are at the core of who I am - this means that I am pro-life and will work to protect the innocent & unborn. Constitution Conservative: what does our U.S. and Georgia Constitution say?  Words have meaning.  Our forefathers, with wisdom from the Almighty, wrote documents that have lasted the ages enshrining our Rights.  The government did not give, nor can they take our Rights away. Fiscal Conservative: I will lead on the budget to give you and your family your dollars back  and eliminate the State Income Tax. Per capita spending in Georgia is lowest in the country. I will work to spend wisely and balance the budget each year.

ga-house-22-2026-r-1.bio: Jordan Ridley is a proud Georgia conservative, lifelong Cherokee County resident, and a proven Republican leader who has dedicated his life to serving his community and defending the values that make Georgia strong. In 2024, Jordan served as a local advocate for President Donald Trump’s re-election in Georgia, speaking with both grassroots groups and the national media—including The New York Times—about President Trump’s record, grassroots support, and the high stakes facing Georgia and the country in the 2024 election.

ga-house-23-2026-r-1.name: Bill Fincher
ga-house-23-2026-r-1.bio: I have spent my career upholding the law, managing budgets, and serving the people of Georgia with integrity. Now I am running to make sure our state government does the same by protecting taxpayers, defending freedom, and keeping Cherokee County the best place to live, work, and raise a family. I was born and raised here in Cherokee County, this is home. I’ve served as an FBI agent, a prosecutor, and a community leader, and I know how to bring people together to solve problems. I’m not a politician, I’m a public servant and consensus builder.”
ga-house-23-2026-r-1._note: Holds the seat Mandi Ballinger resigned from. The district-keyed incumbent lookup filed this candidate under Mandi Ballinger's member record, which showed on Mandi Ballinger's own page as "Running for ... in 2026". Pinned to their real record.

ga-house-24-2026-r-1.name: Carter Barrett
ga-house-24-2026-r-1.bio: arter has served his community and Forsyth County on numerous boards and organizations for over 30 years — including Sawnee Community Center, Northside Hospital Foundation, United Way of Forsyth County, GNFCC, Forsyth County Chamber, The Place of Forsyth, Peachtree Parkway Improvement District and Pups with a Purpose. The Georgia House of Representatives has also recognized Carter for his contributions and service to Forsyth County.

ga-house-25-2026-r-2.bio: Todd Jones is a husband, a dad, and community leader; not a career politician.  He has proudly served the constituents of Georgia House District 25 since January 2017.

ga-house-28-2026-r-1.name: Brent Cox
ga-house-28-2026-r-1.bio: Brent Cox is a family man, coach, and hardworking entrepreneur who has owned, managed, and led business ventures for over 24 years. After attending Milton High School, he graduated from the University of Georgia in 1994. Cox then went on to have a successful career in the food service industry where he designed, engineered, and sold ventilation hood systems to chain restaurants on a global scale for over two decades. Cox has also been involved in remediation work for the state and real estate acquisitions. Now, he serves as the President of Simple Mission in Cumming, a company that serves as a manufacturer’s representative in the food service industry.

ga-house-29-2026-r-2.name: Matt Dubnik
ga-house-29-2026-r-2.bio: Born right here in Gainesville, I am a conservative Republican, small business owner, father, husband and someone who is active in my community. I have had a desire to serve my community since I was a young boy. That’s why my responsibility as a public servant for Gainesville and Hall County is not one I take lightly.

ga-house-30-2026-r-1.name: Derrick McCollum
ga-house-30-2026-r-1.bio: Prior to being elected to the Georgia House of Representatives in 2022, Derrick served his community as a firefighter and EMT for Hall County for seventeen years and Habersham County for two years.  In addition to serving as a Majority Deputy Whip, Derrick currently serves on the following committees: Transportation, Secretary; Natural Resources & Environment; Defense & Veterans Affairs

ga-house-35-2026-d-1.name: Lisa Gayle Campbell
ga-house-35-2026-d-1.bio: Lisa Campbell was elected as the first woman to Represent Georgia in House District 35. Donate to her campaign for reelection. Sign up to receive her newsletter and stay in the know about legislative issues in Georgia, Town Hall events, and community activities.

ga-house-39-2026-d-1.name: Terry Cummings
ga-house-39-2026-d-1.bio: I grew up on the principle that America is a “melting pot” of different races, cultures, religions, nationalities working together to realize the “American Dream”. I believe all Georgians deserve the opportunity to achieve the dream. As your next state representative, I will work to: -Preserve the rights of all Georgian’s regardless of race, nationality, religion, or sexual orientation.

ga-house-61-2026-d-2.name: Mekyah McQueen
ga-house-61-2026-d-2.bio:
Mcqueen Portraits.png

Mekyah McQueen is an educator, a fierce advocate for youth and families, and an unwavering problem solver. She is the strongest advocate to represent District 61 in the Georgia State House and fight for our Democratic values - a well-funded public education system, protecting our right to vote, and expanding Medicaid.

ga-house-65-2026-d-1.bio: As your State Representative, I've been committed to advancing policies that strengthen our communities and ensure the safety and well-being of all Georgians. In 2025, we achieved significant tax cut, public safety and education gains. I have been outspoken and out front leading the fight for lower prices and lower taxes.  I co-sponsored successful legislation in Fulton and Coweta counties to lower school property taxes for seniors.  We are actively working on legislation to reel in out-of-control auto insurance rates. My primary focus is to "upskill" District 65 for the economy of the future. I want to make sure our youth have access to the education and vocational training they need to prosper.  We need access to a quality job market and substantial business opportunities, so our families and communities grow. We also need financial security for our seniors so they can age in place and leave a legacy in our communities that we can build upon.

ga-house-66-2026-d-2.bio:
Representative Kimberly Alexander was elected to the Georgia General Assembly in 2012. Representative Alexander serves District 66 which encompasses Douglas County and the Southeast section of Paulding County. District 66 is a newly drawn map and Representative Alexander made history by becoming the first African-American female elected to serve the District in Paulding and the first African-American female that lives in Douglas to be elected and serve in Douglas.

In the Georgia General Assembly, Representative Alexander sits on the following Committees; Code Revision, Intragovernmental Coordination, Motor Vehicle, Banks & Banking and Legislative & Congressional Reapportionment.

challenger-timothy-fleming-sos-2026.bio: Tim Fleming is a proven conservative, small business owner, and a champion for election integrity with a strong record of fighting for Georgia. As former Chief of Staff to Gov. Kemp and Deputy Secretary of State under then Sec. Kemp, Tim took on Stacey Abrams' election schemes, cracked down on voter fraud, and streamlined professional licensing. Now serving in the State House, he continues to lead efforts to secure our elections and cut red tape. As Secretary of State, Tim will keep fighting to protect our elections, simplify licensing, and defend Georgia values.

ga-senate-18-2026-r-2.name: Steven McNeel
ga-senate-18-2026-r-2._note: Holds the seat John Kennedy resigned from. The district-keyed incumbent lookup filed this candidate under John Kennedy's member record, which showed on John Kennedy's own page as "Running for ... in 2026". Pinned to their real record.

ga-house-1-2026-d-1.name: Steven "Diz" Disbrow
ga-house-1-2026-d-1.bio:
Since moving here 7 years ago, I’ve fallen in love with the area and now I simply refuse to leave. This really is a fantastic place to live, and the views are pretty spectacular too.

But, of course, things could always be better. Healthcare, food and job security, infrastructure, affordability and economic development are all things that the folks under the Golden Dome seem to have forgotten about. At least when it comes to NW Georgia.

I’m running for the Georgia House Of Representatives in order to represent YOU and make sure your voices are heard and our needs as a community are met.

ga-house-9-2026-r-1.name: Chris Dockery
ga-house-9-2026-r-1.bio:
A proven public servant, Dockery is currently serving his 4th term as Lumpkin County Commission Chairman. He has a proven track record of working with citizens, fellow Commissioners, and county and community leaders to move Lumpkin County forward in a positive direction. In his role, he is also active in the Association of County Commissioners. He holds numerous leadership positions in ACCG, including, serving as a member of ACCG’s Georgia Legislative Policy Council and serve as District II representative on the Board of Managers, representing counties across North Georgia. He also continues to serve as a member UNG Corps Advisory Committee, as a lifetime member of the North Georgia Corps of Cadets Association, and as a member of the Dahlonega Sunrise Rotary Club. He previously served as board member of the Development Authority of Lumpkin County and on the Lumpkin County Water and Sewerage Authority from 2008-2012.

 

Dockery and his wife, Krista, have three children. They are active members of Town Creek Baptist Church. Outside of his numerous roles, he enjoys tournament bass fishing with his son.

ga-house-15-2026-d-1.name: Lauren Jones
ga-house-15-2026-d-1.bio:
Transparency and Accountability
Government should answer to the people — not operate behind closed doors. I believe in honest leadership, clear communication, and real accountability at every level of public service. Our community deserves transparency, responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars, and leaders who will always put the public first.

Healthcare and Immigration Reform
I believe Georgia families deserve a state government that tackles real problems with practical solutions. On healthcare, that means expanding access to primary care, mental health services, and rural healthcare so families are not forced to drive hours or wait too long to get the care they need. We should support policies that strengthen our healthcare workforce, invest in local hospitals and clinics, and help make care more affordable for working families. On immigration, we need a balanced approach that upholds the law, strengthens public safety, supports legal pathways to work, and recognizes the role hardworking people play in Georgia’s economy. I believe we can lead with both compassion and common sense while building a stronger, safer, and healthier Georgia.

People First
I believe leadership begins with people first. Government should never lose sight of the families, workers, and neighbors it is meant to serve. When we lead with compassion, integrity, and common sense, we build a stronger community and a better future for everyone.
        
Affordability
I believe affordability is about protecting the quality of life our families work hard to build. No one should feel like they are falling behind just trying to pay for housing, groceries, healthcare, and everyday necessities. I will fight for practical solutions that ease financial pressure, strengthen opportunity, and help working families get ahead.

ga-house-27-2026-d-1.name: Jay Kirkland
ga-house-27-2026-d-1.bio:
With a deep-rooted commitment to Georgia's District 27, I have spent my career enriching the lives of families in communities like ours. My journey is fueled by a passion for service and a belief that every citizen deserves a voice in the halls of power.

As we face new challenges in a rapidly evolving legislative landscape, my focus remains steadfast on ensuring safety, fairness, and opportunity for all. I believe in practical, community-driven solutions that prioritize safety, infrastructure, and sustainable growth for future generations.

Leadership is about listening more than speaking. Over the next months, I'm working to meet thousands of neighbors, hearing your concerns, and understanding the unique needs of our district. It is your resilience and spirit that drives this campaign forward every single day.

I am running for the Georgia State House because I believe we can build a better tomorrow through collaboration and transparency. Our district deserves a representative who is not just present, but actively engaged in moving us toward a more prosperous and inclusive future.

Let's Do Better Together for Georgia.

ga-house-54-2026-r-1.name: Greg Miller
ga-house-54-2026-r-1.bio:
Running for office was never in Greg’s long-term plan but when he experienced his own property taxes rising dramatically, he felt a call to continue serving his community — this time in the State House. Greg has heard from parents worried about schools, families stretched thin by rising costs, and people who feel like no one in the legislature is focused on the issues that actually affect their day-to-day lives. 

 

Greg is stepping up because he believes this district deserves serious, thoughtful leadership, not more partisan politics. He’s running as a common-sense conservative who wants to get back to the basics: making life more affordable, improving schools, supporting families, and keeping communities safe.

ga-house-61-2026-r-1.name: Damita Bishop
ga-house-61-2026-r-1.bio:
Justice advocate, Author
Co-founder of F.A.I.R
Candidate for Georgia State Rep 2026

ga-house-65-2026-r-1.name: Gordon W. Rolle Jr.
ga-house-65-2026-r-1.bio:
Dr. Gordon W. Rolle Jr. has called South Fulton home since 1976. A U.S. Air Force veteran and lifelong educator, his commitment to this community is not a campaign promise — it's nearly five decades of showing up.

Since 1990, Dr. Rolle has dedicated his career to building workforce-ready skills for students and adults in transition. He and his wife, Dr. Sonia Francis-Rolle, have led aviation career awareness and job-skills programs in South Fulton that have produced NASA interns — connecting young people in District 65 to careers they never thought possible.

Off the campaign trail, Dr. Rolle has served as President of the Ponderosa Neighbor Association, participated in Fulton County citizen police and sheriff academies, advocated for government accountability at the local level, and helped build the Atlanta Aerotropolis Alliance Education Collective. He currently serves as Vice Chair of the FCRP and Chair for District 65 on the Georgia Republican State Committee.

District 65 isn't just where he's running. It's where he has lived his values for 50 years.

ga-house-67-2026-r-1.name: Daniel Cook
ga-house-67-2026-r-1.bio:
Daniel Cook is a lifelong resident of District 67 and a proud product of Coweta County. A graduate of Trinity Christian School in Sharpsburg, Daniel went on to earn his degree from Georgia Tech with Highest Honors in Economics, along with minors in Political Science and History.

His experience spans the public and private sectors—from working in Congressman Drew Ferguson's office on constituent casework, to supporting Governor Kemp's internship program tracking legislation for the University System of Georgia.

Most recently, Daniel served as the Regional Field Director for Congressman Buddy Carter's Senate campaign. He also spent the summer working as a counselor at a children's summer camp.

When he's not working, Daniel enjoys spending time with his fiancée Jessica, who hails from Ireland. Together they love exploring Georgia and beyond.

Daniel is running because he believes Georgia deserves leadership that rewards hard work, strengthens families, and creates real opportunity for the next generation.

ga-house-73-2026-d-1.name: Tim Wilkinson
ga-house-73-2026-d-1.bio:
Hello, I'm Tim Wilkinson and I'm running for GA House District 73. I am married and a father of five with nine wonderful grandchildren. My wife Sheila and I have called Georgia home for almost 29 years. I retired from the U.S. Postal Service after 33 years, where I often served as a Union Representative for the National Association of Letter Carriers.


I currently work two part-time blue-collar jobs to help make ends meet. I am not an attorney, realtor, or rich businessman. In fact, like most Georgians, my only property ownership is a primary residence, our home. I work and live, paycheck to paycheck, just like millions of my fellow Americans.


I have no financial interest in any businesses. My only interest is in serving the citizens of District 73, and the great state of Georgia. I hope to secure our community's safety and prosperity, and to ensure our continued success with dignity and respect for all, and the dream of a better future. 


I am running for this office to help restore civility, dignity, and honesty to our political system. I will attempt to effect positive progressive change and move Georgia forward into a prosperous new century. As a legislator, I intend to scour the country for any legislation that improves the lives of Georgians, being proactive instead of reactive.

ga-house-100-2026-r-2.name: Josh Clark
ga-house-100-2026-r-2.bio:
I will hold fast to the foundational principles of faith, family, and freedom that built this country. With the support of my neighbors and friends, I look forward to serving as your next State Representative for the 100th District. I promise to cast a vision and craft policies that help keep our Northeast Georgia community—and our beloved state of Georgia—strong, free, and safe.

Josh looks forward to giving back to the community where he grew up. He knows this community well, having represented it for two terms before leaving unopposed 12 years ago. Josh has coached volleyball, football, cross country, and basketball. He has also volunteered in many capacities including serving on the foundation board at Lanier High School. Over the past two decades, his family has actively served both at Sugar Hill Church and, in recent years, at Christ Place Church, where Josh serves in the high school ministry. He also owns businesses in the district, including a nutritional distribution company with his wife, Chelsey, and Clark-It Realty, a full-service real estate brokerage that he runs with his daughter Moriah.

ga-house-100-2026-d-1.name: Jennifer Ambler
ga-house-100-2026-d-1.bio:
Jennifer Ambler has lived in Forsyth County for close to 6 years and has fully adopted Georgia as her new home. Originally from Florida, she graduated from the University of Florida with a BA in Political Science and Economics, and after college worked as a Mathematics Teacher at a high school in Philadelphia as part of Teach For America. She then moved to NYC, starting her own tax preparation company and working in musical theater, but she missed warmth and backyards so she and her husband Adam moved to Forsyth in 2020.
 
Jennifer has always had a passion for politics and believes that government should be a tool to help people live their best lives. Starting from being active in her high school's Youth in Government Club to volunteering for Warnock and Abrams as well as being on the Executive Board of the Forsyth Democrats, Jennifer has always been a strong liberal who stands up for the values she believes in - equality, freedom, and opportunity. 

In addition to her day job, she is also a political comedian, writing parody songs about current affairs. Check out her work at parodyinblue.com

ga-house-121-2026-d-1.name: Eric Gisler
ga-house-121-2026-d-1._note: Holds the seat Marcus Wiedower resigned from. The district-keyed incumbent lookup filed this candidate under Marcus Wiedower's member record, which showed on Marcus Wiedower's own page as "Running for ... in 2026". Pinned to their real record.

ga-senate-21-2026-r-1._note: Holds the seat Brandon Beach resigned from. The district-keyed incumbent lookup filed this candidate under Brandon Beach's member record, which showed on Brandon Beach's own page as "Running for ... in 2026". Pinned to their real record.

ga-senate-35-2026-d-3._note: Holds the seat Jason Esteves resigned from. The district-keyed incumbent lookup filed this candidate under Jason Esteves's member record, which showed on Jason Esteves's own page as "Running for ... in 2026". Pinned to their real record.

ga-senate-45-2026-d-1._note: Goes by his middle name; the ballot reads "Scott Tippetts". The quoted called name is what the results pages match on to link him to his profile — plain "Anthony Tippetts" does not match and un-links him.
ga-senate-45-2026-d-1.name: Scott Tippetts

ga-house-6-2026-d-1.bio:
I will strive to give my neighbors, friends, and family of District 6 the representation they deserve at the capitol. My passion is to fight for each and every resident to have access to medical insurance, quality medical and mental healthcare, and top-notch education at every level! 

I will also push for true freedom and bodily autonomy for all! This is what government can do for its citizens and what I know my neighbors, friends, and family expect and deserve!

ga-senate-42-2026-d-0.name: Eric Lee
ga-senate-42-2026-d-0.bio: Reverend Lee is a dedicated husband of 33 years and the father of 5 children. His wife, Meik Lee, is a respected Speech Pathologist in the Newton County School System for over 25 years and shares his dedication to public service. Reverend Lee is running for State Senate because he believes our communities deserve leadership that is both principled and practical. Reverend Lee offers leadership that understands the challenges families face every day. He is committed to creating opportunity for all that addresses rising costs and economic development to education and quality of life, he is focused on solutions that strengthen families, support local communities, and move District 42 forward.

ga-house-13-2026-d-1.name: Vincent Mendes
ga-house-13-2026-d-1.bio:
After 19 years with the same incumbent, I believe it’s time for leadership that is rooted right here at home. The needs of our families, small businesses, and neighborhoods should be the focus… not just decisions made in Atlanta.

I don’t claim to have every answer. What I bring is real, lived experience: as a small business owner, a healthcare provider, a parent of three who have gone through our local schools, and a proud resident of Rome for the past 14 years.

Every day, I hear the concerns of our neighbors… in my office, at church, and at local events. And I believe that listening isn’t just part of the job, it is THE MOST important part.

This campaign won’t be easy. But it’s worth it. This district deserves a voice that shows up, works hard, and stays connected to the people it serves.

ga-house-14-2026-d-1.bio:
Bella Bautista was born and raised in Cartersville as the daughter of small business owners. She grew up
watching her family work long hours, make sacrifices, and rely on faith and perseverance to build a better life.

Bella did not grow up wealthy or politically connected. She does not come from a political dynasty, and her
path was not paved by an elite university or a famous last name. Everything she has built came through hard
work, faith, and the support of people who believed in her.

Like many people across District 14, Bella knows what it is like to watch grocery bills, utility costs, housing
expenses, and everyday necessities become harder to afford. She understands the pressure of trying to make
every dollar stretch because she lives with those same pressures.

As a nonprofit leader and community organizer, Bella has spent years bringing people together and fighting
for the issues her community cares about. She has stood with neighbors demanding responsible growth,
protection for local land, personal privacy, better mental health care, and greater accountability from
government. When residents felt ignored, Bella kept showing up.

Her decision to run is rooted in faith. Bella believes she was called by God to serve her community, and she
sees representing District 14 as the next step in answering that call.

Bella is not running to become a career politician. She is running to serve the community that raised her and
make sure everyday people have someone at the Capitol who understands their struggles, shares their
concerns, and never forgets who she works for.

ga-house-18-2026-d-1.bio: Pat Rhudy is the Democratic candidate for GA House District 18. Some of her top issues include civic engagement, marijuana legalization, and healthcare.

ga-house-19-2026-d-1.bio: Cynthia Starke-Jones is a dedicated educator and community advocate who has spent over two decades serving the families of Georgia. With a deep commitment to public service, she has been a tireless voice for affordable healthcare, strong public schools, and accessible housing. As a former teacher, Cynthia understands firsthand the challenges facing our education system and is prepared to fight for common-sense solutions that put families first in the State House.

ga-house-9-2026-d-2.bio:
Our country was built on a promise: work hard, keep your nose to the grindstone, and your children will have a better life. That promise is broken.

It’s broken because the folks under the Gold Dome listen to big-dollar donors instead of their constituents. They’ve sacrificed livability for profitability. Georgia families pay the price.

It doesn’t require a tax increase to fix it. This year alone, Georgia will give away $2.5 billion in tax revenues to data center companies and get less than $400 million back. That money could rebuild the promise.

ga-senate-9-2026-r-1.bio:
I'm not a career politician. I'm a Gwinnett neighbor who believes that government works best when it's transparent, accountable, and focused on results — not promises. That's the standard I'll hold myself to, every single day in the Georgia Senate.

I know this journey comes with great responsibility, and I am committed to listening, learning, and working hard for our community every step of the way.

ga-senate-44-2026-r-1.name: Ngozi Orabueze
ga-senate-44-2026-r-1.bio: Dr. Orabueze, APRN, has spent her career at the bedside of patients and the heart of her community. Now she's stepping forward to bring clinical compassion and community-driven advocacy to the Georgia State Senate.

ga-house-24-2026-d-1.bio:
I grew up in south Georgia and have lived in Forsyth County for six years. I don’t believe that billionaires should be controlling our politics. 

Our government should care more about its citizens than foreign wars. Medical debt should not be one of the highest contributors of household bankruptcy. 

Our veterans deserve the best healthcare possible.  Serving in our government should not increase your personal wealth. Animals should not suffer for human convenience or profit.

I am running to serve in our state legislature to make Georgia a better place for all of us.

ga-house-26-2026-d-1.bio:
In my roles as mother, disability advocate, health insurance advocate, and animal rescue foster mom, I’ve developed two common threads in my work:

Service. Protection of others.

The issues we face in our district and state are complex. Voters deserve a leader who knows how to put service first. A leader who will not back down when protecting rights for all.

While it is important to collaborate with people of all political backgrounds, I will never compromise my integrity or the people I represent. Serving and protecting others has been my life’s work. This meaningful work has also led to some of my greatest joys.

Divisions have deepened. It is an uncertain time for many Georgians. Our representatives have put politics over people for far too long.

As a public servant, I will always put you first. As a leader, I will fight for you and your family.

My name is Meredith Greene. I am running for Georgia House District 26 in Forsyth County. I am a lifelong advocate. It’s time for me to advocate for you.

ga-house-36-2026-d-1.name: Luc "Luke" Noiset
ga-house-36-2026-d-1.bio:
I am a professor of economics. I study the role of government in the economy. I want to
be an elected official who keeps my constituents fully informed with facts. All of us want
strong and safe cities and towns and good public services. When voters are informed
they will mostly agree on what the government can do.

ga-house-58-2026-r-1.bio:
FULTON COUNTY REPUBLICAN PARTY/ DELEGATE.
TRUMPFORCE 47 CAPITAL.
CONSERVATIVE

ga-house-58-2026-d-1.bio: My name is Mathewos Samson, and I'm a community organizer, democratic socialist, and lifelong Atlantan. I'm running for Georgia House District 58 because Georgia has become unaffordable for regular working people like you and me. Housing, utilities, and the overall cost of living are through the roof, and our politicians are too beholden to corporate donors to stand up for us in the face of this crisis. It’s time to bring working people who reject the bribes of developers and billionaires into the state capitol, with no corporate strings attached. Only we can build a more democratic, equitable, and just society that works for everyone.

ga-house-64-2026-r-1.bio:
I am running for State Representative to ensure our community is safe, supported, and respected. Our state faces significant challenges, and I am committed to delivering common-sense leadership that puts people first. My platform focuses on these key priorities:
 
- Public Safety: I will support law enforcement and invest in crime prevention to ensure every person feels safe in Georgia.

- Education & Well-being: I will advocate for stronger anti-bullying protections for students.  I will strive to increase more support for parents and teachers to gain more control over rebellious children.  My goal is to expand access to mental health and drug treatment services.

- Housing & Homelessness: I support community-based solutions for homelessness and will fight for affordable housing. For seniors, I propose capping rent increases and scaling rent to be based on an apartment's square footage (e.g., $900 per month for 900 sq. ft of rental space).

- Economic Relief: I will endeavor to ease the financial burden on families and seniors.  I will work to reduce property taxes, cut wasteful spending, lower medical costs, and reform HOA practices to prevent exorbitant fines.

I love Georgia and believe in a government that works for its citizens. This campaign is about our collective future.  I invite you to join the movement by volunteering, displaying a yard sign, spreading the word or making a donation.

Together, we can restore safety and create opportunity for everyone.

ga-house-71-2026-d-2.bio:
I’m excited to announce my campaign for Georgia House District 71, and I’m inviting you to be a part of this grassroots movement. This campaign isn’t about one person—it’s about bringing our community together to create real opportunities and solutions for the families who live here.

With more than 20 years of public service and as a mother and grandmother, I understand the real challenges families face every day. I’m running because I believe our district deserves leadership that listens and works to improve the quality of life for everyone.

Our campaign is focused on three key priorities: 

• Affordability – Helping families keep more of their hard-earned money and addressing the rising cost of living. 

• Workforce Opportunities – Expanding job training and pathways to stable, good-paying careers. 

• Healthcare Access – Ensuring individuals and families have access to affordable, quality healthcare.

But a campaign like this can only succeed with the support of dedicated volunteers and community leaders.

ga-house-82-2026-d-1.bio:
Anthony, a native of Griffin, Georgia, graduated from Griffin High School and played football on a scholarship at Fort Valley State College before transferring to Mercer University, where he earned his bachelor's degree while studying full-time. He then worked in the public school system as a paraprofessional and teacher, specializing in middle grades Business Education and Computer Science. 

Anthony is also the author of A Man Lost, available on Amazon, and earned an MBA from Strayer University, graduating Magna Cum Laude. He is the proud father of three children—Xzavier, Christopher, and Ebony—and grandfather to five grandsons and one granddaughter: Aydin, Brycen, Christopher Jr., Mariah, Dash, and Kash.

Anthony Dickson believes District 82 deserves a leader who values transparency and is dedicated to advocating for its citizens. Together, we can build a more inclusive and united future for District 82. Get involved and make your voice count.
